mechanisms.name: Default privateKey.rotationPolicy becomes Always — effect on cert-manager/mesh-root-ca (the trust anchor)
mechanisms.mechanism: Silent rotation of the CA key would have been the dangerous case, because the leaf ca.crt values and ledger's ssl_client_certificate trust this CA.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The prod overlay patches in rotationPolicy: Never, and Argo deploys the prod overlay, so the CA key is explicitly pinned. The rendered from/to output contains an identical mesh-root-ca with rotationPolicy: Never. Caveat: Never only protects the key; the root renews on its own schedule (duration 8760h, renewBefore 720h) with the same key, and that is unchanged by this upgrade.
citedEvidence: rendered/from.yaml and rendered/to.yaml contain an identical mesh-root-ca with rotationPolicy: Never
pki render marked "identical in from and to"
assumptions: The repo matches live state (the repo is declared complete but not runtime-verified)
missingEvidence: Live-cluster confirmation that mesh-root-ca has rotationPolicy: Never, not just the repo
recommendedValidation: Confirm the live mesh-root-ca has rotationPolicy: Never, not just the repo

mechanisms.name: Default privateKey.rotationPolicy becomes Always — effect on payments/ledger-tls and payments/checkout-tls (leaf certificates) and their consumers
mechanisms.mechanism: Neither leaf Certificate sets rotationPolicy, so on 1.18.0 each renewal generates a new ECDSA P-256 key (on 1.17.2 they keep the key). Nothing happens at upgrade time; a new key appears at the first renewal after the upgrade (about day 20 with duration 720h / renewBefore 240h), or on a manual cmctl renew or Secret deletion. Consumer risks: checkout runs curl every 30s re-reading the files; if the kubelet ..data symlink swap lands between the cert and key reads, curl gets a mismatched pair and one 30s iteration fails ("ledger call failed", no crash) — small window and self-healing. Ledger's nginx reads cert/key only at startup/reload with no reloader, so it never picks up a renewed certificate and would serve an expired cert after 720h whether the key rotated or not (pre-existing latent bug that the rotation default makes more visible); under Always, an nginx reload or restart racing the symlink swap could read a new cert with an old key and refuse to start — probability is low.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The CRD schema diff only changes description text and sets no CRD default, so Argo sees no drift. The issuer (CA issuer signing from the root Secret) does not depend on leaf key continuity, and neither do algorithm or size, so issuance will succeed. Checkout picks up new credentials with no restart. Impact on ledger is bounded: peers verify chains against the CA (ca.crt), not pinned leaf keys. No pinning found in env/ (no leaf public key, SPKI hash or fingerprint pinning, no allow-lists, no other consumers of these Secrets), so within the repo key rotation is semantically harmless.
citedEvidence: prod overlay only patches ledger replicas (now 2)
CRD schema diff only changes description text and sets no CRD default
Nothing in env/ pins the leaf public key, SPKI hash or fingerprint

Staging rehearsal: upgrade, then cmctl renew ledger-tls checkout-tls -n payments; verify the Secret gets a new key (compare tls.key public key before and after), checkout can reach ledger on the next loop iterations, and ledger behaviour (does nginx keep serving the old cert or fail); run nginx -s reload and confirm it succeeds

Decide how ledger nginx picks up renewed certs (reloader annotation, sidecar, or rolling restart on renewal); fix regardless of the upgrade, ideally before the first post-upgrade renewal at about day 20
Watch the first real renewals in prod and alert on handshake failures from ledger to checkout
Confirm no other Argo apps or operators create Certificates with default policy and depend on key continuity

mechanisms.name: cert-manager install values / DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways feature gate (and other rendered differences)
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: Not affected: the cert-manager install values
mechanisms.mechanism: values.yaml sets no config.featureGates, so the gate DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways is on by default in 1.18.0. Other rendered differences (RBAC split of challenge roles, new CRD fields, webhook probe port name) are out of scope for this change.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The rendered controller args show no feature-gate flags in either version. The other rendered differences have no obvious link to the mesh, which uses no ACME.
citedEvidence: rendered controller args show no feature-gate flags in either version

overall.recommendation: Proceed with conditions: safe to proceed after the listed checks. Treat the default flip as acceptable; optionally set privateKey.rotationPolicy: Always explicitly on the two leaf Certificates (or Never if zero behaviour change is wanted) rather than using the feature gate; do not rely on config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false; fix the ledger reload gap as a separate prerequisite.
overall.quote: I rate it "safe to proceed after the checks below", not "no impact".
